question.text: A Cat III AIF scheme that accepts investors other than accredited investors must ensure a minimum investment of:

answer.text: Rs. 1 crore per investor (except for Accredited Investors)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, minimum investment from every non-Accredited investor should be Rs. 1 crore. The Trap: Rs. 25/50 lakh thresholds apply to specific employee/associates, not general investors. Rs. 5 crore is incorrect. Cross-Exam Context: Accredited Investors enjoy a carve-out under the Third Amendment Regulations. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Accredited Investor status must be verified by a recognised accreditation agency — keep certificates on file.
